stages.a: Wild white fluff grows on top of the block.
stages.v: A healthy block grows fluff on top, but only if it was incubated no warmer than about 18 °C and not held too long. Don't be afraid of the fluff.

stages.a: Amber droplets bead on the fluff.
stages.v: The amber droplets are the giveaway that the block is about to pin. Open now: snip the corners or cut the top off.

stages.a: A carpet of golden pin nodules covers the top.
stages.v: Waiting for the carpet is the traditional way, but a little late: the fruit comes out stringy and gnarly. Once the carpet changes, it is ready in about 1.5-2 days.

stages.a: Long, slender stems lift small round caps.
stages.v: Fast in the fruit room, like shiitake. 18-24 °C, and warmer is faster. Lights on once the carpet forms.

stages.a: The caps are still held to the stems by the veil.
stages.v: Harvest just before the cap breaks away from the edge of the stem and flattens.

stages.a: The caps break from the stems and flatten. The veil is left as a ring.

labels.a: Aerial mycelium on the block top.
labels.v: A lack of fluff is a warning sign.
The giveaway that the block is about to pin.

labels.a: Golden pin nodules across the top.
labels.v: Waiting for the pin carpet is a little late: the fruit comes out stringy.

labels.a: Long, slender stems in a tight bunch.
The veil still joins the cap edge to the stem.
labels.v: Pick just before the cap breaks away from the stem.

labels.a: The cap breaks away from the stem and flattens.
